title: Customer chip opens a dropdown with a 'Search customer' field and a scrollable customer list
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Several customers exist in the shop.
steps: 1. Click the Customer filter chip.
2. Look at the top of the dropdown panel and the list below it.
3. Look at the bottom of the panel.
expected: 1. A dropdown panel opens under the Customer chip.
2. A search input with the placeholder 'Search customer' is at the top, already focused so you can type right away.
3. Below it is a scrollable list of customer names.
4. A 'Clear selection' action is shown at the bottom of the panel.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 #10 (11842:14236 - list pattern also evidenced in final mobile sheets #20/#21)
notes: Whether the input is auto-focused on open is shown as focused in the design - VIU-confirm in the build.

title: Typing in the customer search narrows the list to matching names
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. Several customers with different names exist.
steps: 1. Type part of one customer's name into the 'Search customer' field (for example the first few letters).
2. Watch the list while you type.
expected: 1. The customer list narrows as you type, showing only names that match what you entered.
2. Customers that do not match are removed from the list.
3. Deleting the text brings the full list back.

title: Selecting customers adds removable tags in the dropdown input area and checkmarks in the list
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. At least three customers exist.
steps: 1. Click one customer in the list.
2. Click a second and a third customer.
3. Look at the input area at the top of the dropdown and at the list rows.
expected: 1. Each selected customer appears as a tag (small chip) with an x in the input area at the top of the dropdown.
2. Each selected customer's row in the list shows a checkmark on the right.
3. Long customer names on tags are shortened with an ellipsis (for example 'Texas Truck And Aut...').
4. You can keep selecting as many customers as needed - there is no selection limit.
design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 #11 (11854:19595 - token pattern also in final mobile frame #23 11884:16383)
spec_ref: Filters (no Jira epic) (S3-R3; S3-R4; §4 Key Decisions (no selection limit)) [spec v1.6 2026-07-28]
notes: The design also shows a clear-all (x) circle icon at the top right of the token field - VIU-confirm whether the build has it and what it clears (visual detail beyond the spec text).

title: Clicking the x on a customer tag removes just that customer from the selection
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open.
3. Two or more customers are selected (their tags are visible in the input area).
steps: 1. Click the x on one selected customer's tag.
2. Look at the tags, the list and the work order table.
expected: 1. That customer's tag disappears from the input area.
2. The checkmark next to that customer in the list is removed.
3. The other selected customers keep their tags and checkmarks.
4. The table updates to no longer include that customer's work orders.

title: The table shows only work orders belonging to any of the selected customers
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page on the All tab.
3. At least two customers each have at least one work order, and a third customer's work orders also exist (seed ZZAUTOTEST data if needed).
steps: 1. Open the Customer filter and select two customers.
2. Look at the Customer column in the work order table.
expected: 1. The table shows only work orders whose customer is one of the two selected customers.
2. Work orders belonging to any other customer are hidden.
3. The table updates in real time as you make the selections (no apply button on desktop).
spec_ref: Filters (no Jira epic) (S3-R6; S2-R6 (real-time pattern)) [spec v1.6 2026-07-28]
notes: Tech plan 2026-07-29 (engineering intent - confirm live at the wording/behaviour pass): 'Customer' here means the customer ACCOUNT/company shown in the grid's Customer column, not the contact person on the work order (G3) - seed test data accordingly.

title: Clear selection in the Customer dropdown removes all selected customers
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page.
3. Two or more customers are selected in the Customer filter and the table is filtered.
steps: 1. Open the Customer dropdown (if not already open).
2. Click 'Clear selection' at the bottom of the dropdown.
3. Look at the tags, the list and the table.
expected: 1. All customer tags are removed from the input area.
2. All checkmarks in the list are removed.
3. The Customer filter is removed and the table shows work orders of all customers again.
4. Other active filters (if any) are not affected.

title: Clicking outside the Customer dropdown closes it and the selections remain
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Work Orders page with the Customer dropdown open and two customers selected.
steps: 1. Click anywhere outside the dropdown.
2. Look at the Customer chip and the table.
3. Click the Customer chip again to reopen the dropdown.
expected: 1. The dropdown closes when you click outside it.
2. The Customer chip stays in the active (blue) state showing the selection and the table stays filtered.
3. When reopened, the selected customers' tags are still visible in the input area.

title: Customer search with no matching name shows a no-results message in the list
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.

steps: 1. Type a string that matches no customer name (for example 'zzzqqq').
2. Look at the list area of the dropdown.
expected: 1. The list shows a message saying there are no results (instead of an empty gap).

design_ref: design-notes.md B.1 (no-results list state not drawn in the final frames)

title: A customer with no open work orders is still listed; filtering by them returns an empty result
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).

title: A deactivated technician does not appear in the Lead Technician filter list
permissions_required: Any signed-in user with access to the Work Orders page; an admin account to deactivate a test staff member (the spec defines no role-based differences - OQ-4).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A test technician (ZZAUTOTEST) exists and is visible in the Lead Technician filter list.
3. That test technician is then made inactive/deactivated in staff administration (restore them afterwards).
steps: 1. On the Work Orders page, open the Lead Technician filter.
2. Search for the deactivated technician's name.
3. Look at the list.
expected: 1. The deactivated technician is NOT shown in the filter list.
2. Active technicians are still listed normally.
notes: How the app marks a staff member inactive is env-specific - use the staff administration screen; restore the staff member's state after the test (Standing Rule 5). Tech plan 2026-07-29 (engineering intent - confirm live at the wording/behaviour pass): the technician list shows only active, clockable staff for the CURRENT location; after switching location, selected technicians who are not in the new location silently drop from the chip (section 4-3.2).
